paper.title: A-Level Physics — Sample Paper A (unofficial practice)
paper.source_note: Written for this platform as a practice paper in the style of the S6 national examination. Not a NESA paper.

title: A-Level Physics — Sample Paper A
description: 60 minutes. Take g = 9.8 m/s², h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s. Written answers are marked by your teacher.
subject: physics

questions.prompt: The SI unit of magnetic flux is the…
questions.explanation: Magnetic flux is measured in webers (Wb); flux density in teslas.

questions.prompt: Find the period (s) of a simple pendulum of length 1.00 m.
A 20 μF capacitor is charged to 12 V. Find the charge stored in μC.
Find the energy of a photon of frequency $5.0 \times 10^{14}$ Hz, in units of $10^{-19}$ J.

choices.text: the secondary coil has more turns than the primary
the primary coil has more turns than the secondary
both coils have the same number of turns

questions.prompt: A radioactive sample has a mass of 80 g and a half-life of 5 days. What mass (g) remains undecayed after 15 days?
Find the combined resistance (Ω) of 6 Ω and 3 Ω in parallel.
A cell of e.m.f. 12 V and internal resistance 1 Ω is connected to a 5 Ω resistor. Find the current (A).
In the photoelectric effect, increasing the intensity of the light increases the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electrons.
questions.explanation: Maximum KE depends on frequency ($hf - \phi$); intensity changes the *number* of electrons.

questions.prompt: A spring of constant 200 N/m is stretched by 5.0 cm. Find the force (N).
State Lenz's law and explain how it follows from the principle of conservation of energy.
questions.marking_guide: B1: induced current flows in a direction to oppose the change producing it. B1: e.g. magnet pushed into coil → induced pole repels magnet. B1: work must be done against this opposition. B1: that work becomes electrical energy; if the current aided the change, energy would be created from nothing — violating conservation.
questions.explanation: The induced current opposes the change; the work done against it is the source of the electrical energy.

questions.prompt: Explain how an n-type semiconductor is produced, and describe how a p–n junction diode allows current in one direction only.
questions.marking_guide: B1: doping silicon with a pentavalent (group 5) impurity e.g. phosphorus. B1: extra free electrons are majority carriers. B1: forward bias narrows the depletion layer and current flows. B1: reverse bias widens the depletion layer; (almost) no current.
questions.explanation: Pentavalent doping gives free electrons; the depletion layer narrows in forward bias and widens in reverse bias.
